item.title: Version 0.1.0-b11
item.description:
New

  • AMR-WB (G.722.2) — all nine bitrate modes (6.60–23.85 kbit/s), both RFC 4867 payload framings, dynamic payload-type negotiation and a true 16 kHz RTP clock. Decoding uses the AMR-WB codec built into macOS; encoding uses a vendored copy of vo-amrwbenc (Apache-2.0).
  • Receive jitter buffer — reorders by RTP sequence number, fills gaps with silence and smooths relays that batch-deliver packets. Optional per profile, with an adjustable target depth.
  • Call recording — capture a call to a stereo WAV with this client on the left channel and the peer on the right. Can be armed before the call so nothing is missed.
  • Waveform on the call charts — a recorded call now shows its audio alongside the inter-arrival and jitter charts, sharing the same time axis and zoom, with playback and a synced playhead.
  • Shareable HTML export — ⌘E in the chart window writes a single self-contained page with the charts and the recording embedded, so a call can be handed to someone who doesn't have the app.

Fixed

  • Dialer settings that hadn't been saved yet were ignored by inbound calls and by scenarios — both read the last-saved profile. Unsaved edits now apply everywhere.
  • Restored Sparkle auto-update, the .sipcall file association and the app's bundle identifier, which had been dropped from the generated Xcode project.

item.title: Version 0.1.0-b10
item.description:
What’s new in 0.1.0-b10

  • In-app updates. SipClient now checks for new releases automatically and offers to download and install them for you. You can also trigger a check manually from SipClient → Check for Updates…

Updates are signed end-to-end (Apple notarization plus a Sparkle EdDSA signature). If verification ever fails, the update is refused — you’ll never end up running a tampered build.
